title: NastAero: An Open-Source BDF-Native Aeroelastic and Rotor Loads Framework for Certification-Oriented eVTOL Loads Analysis
description:
NastAero is an open-source aeroelastic finite-element framework that reads MSC Nastran bulk-data (BDF) input and integrates fixed-wing static aeroelastic trim (SOL 144, with inertia relief for free-free models) with rotor load models for hover, transition, and rotor-failure cases in a single tested loads path.

The aeroelastic coupling uses a two-G-matrix spline that separates the normalwash and force-transfer roles. Trim is reduced by a Schur complement onto the trim degrees of freedom, so subcases sharing a flight condition reuse one factorization. Rotor loads from blade-element momentum theory and a reduced-order Pitt-Peters-form inflow lag feed the same finite-element model and the load-recovery, envelope, and critical-design-load pipeline, ending in FORCE-card decks.

This release accompanies the submitted manuscripts. The test suite is run in continuous integration on every change; the expected counts are 816 collected / 790 passed / 26 skipped with the solver extras, and 866 collected / 840 passed / 26 skipped with the optional GUI extra. The skipped tests require a third-party proprietary comparison model that is not redistributable and is therefore excluded from this archive.
